seo.metaTitle: Sharpen PNG Online - Free Image Sharpener, No Upload
seo.metaDescription: Sharpen an image in your browser by boosting local contrast around edges. Free, no upload, no limits. Works with PNG, JPG, WebP and BMP.
seo.longDescription: Sharpen PNG strengthens the contrast between each pixel and its neighbors, which makes edges look crisper. The strength setting blends the sharpened result with the original: at 0% the image comes back unchanged, and at 100% the sharpening kernel is applied at full strength. The tool is for images that are already correctly sized and slightly soft — it does not add detail that was never captured, so it cannot rescue a photo that was enlarged too far. Processing happens in your browser and the file is never uploaded.
facts: Runs entirely in your browser: no upload, no server, no signup.
Strength blends the effect with the original; 0% returns the image unchanged.
Too much strength creates bright halos around edges — start low.
Cannot recover detail that was never captured.
Free with no daily limit, no watermark and no account, also for commercial use.
howTo: Drop the image into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
Set the strength: start low, because too much creates bright halos around edges.
Compare the preview against the original by toggling the before and after view.
Download the result, choosing the format in the Download button.

faq.a: No change at all - the tool returns the original image. The effect grows from there, so it is safe to start at the default and lower it if the result looks harsh.

faq.q: Why did my sharpened image develop bright edges?
faq.a: That is the classic halo effect: the kernel pushes extreme values outward along every edge, which makes light outlines and dark outlines around shapes. Lower the strength, or apply it after a light blur, which is the usual way to tame it.

faq.q: Can sharpening add detail that was never there?
faq.a: No. Sharpening works with the pixels that already exist - it raises local contrast around them. If a photo was enlarged far beyond its original size, the missing detail cannot be recovered by sharpening.
No. Decoding, sharpening and encoding all run in your browser tab, so your image stays on your device.
